clue.text: Violent deaths having one cemetery slab

indicators.note: violent suggests something thrown about, so the letters of deaths are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grim inscription recording several brutal killings on a single tombstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Violent' rearranges DEATHS into HEADST; ONE follows, and 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave marker standing at the head of a burial plot is the usual stone slab in a graveyard.

clue.text: Settled practice of dress in a monastery

explanation.surface: Monks' customary routine includes how they clothe themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a regular custom; the other is the robe worn by monks and nuns.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular custom or routine, and the long robe worn by members of a religious order.

clue.text: How everything finishes completely

explanation.surface: A remark on the way all things come to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a sentence, every thing's ends turn up; as an idiom it means thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning the whole thing in the end, and an idiom for thoroughly or utterly.

clue.text: Pop-group reviewed Geri's clips

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the clips are looked at again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic reviews video clips of the singer Geri, from a pop band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' rearranges the ten letters of GERIS CLIPS. Geri Halliwell was a member of this 1990s British girl band.
explanation.definitionFit: A hugely successful 1990s British girl band whose members included Geri Halliwell.

clue.text: For sale: new roof rebuilt with iron content

indicators.note: content, read as contained, puts the iron symbol inside
rebuilt says the roof and its new letter are put together again in a different order

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A property advertisement: freshly reconstructed roof with metal in it, now on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' rearranges N and ROOF into ONOR; FE goes inside it, signalled by 'content'.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods available to buy at a stated price are said to be available on the market.

clue.text: Get rid of slowly due to, for example, change

indicators.note: change tells us the letters are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Removing something gradually because of change, say climate change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges DUE TO plus EG.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease someone out gradually, displacing them bit by bit, means removing them slowly.

clue.text: Monastic head and sailor having some bother

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the crossword sailor

indicators.note: some of the word bother is taken, its opening letters

explanation.surface: A head of monks and a seaman get into a spot of trouble together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks BOT from the start of 'bother'.
explanation.definitionFit: The superior who governs a community of monks holds this title.

clue.text: Some American news-girl

indicators.note: some says only part of the run of words is taken

explanation.surface: A newspaper delivery girl from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes the letters running across 'AmericAN NEws'.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so in crosswords it can stand for any girl.

clue.text: Graduate's in charge of computer language

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate, and Graduate's is BA's, BAS

explanation.surface: A university graduate is put in charge of computer programming.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive gives BA'S, so the S counts.
explanation.definitionFit: An early beginner's programming language, Beginner's All-purpose Symbolic Instruction Code.

clue.text: He had guest perplexed, without a Poet Laureate

indicators.note: perplexed suggests confusion, so the remaining letters are mixed up
without means the letter a is removed from the words before them

explanation.surface: A host's visitor is left baffled, lacking a famous poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops A from HE HAD GUEST, and 'perplexed' rearranges the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: The English poet held the royal laureateship from 1984 until his death in 1998.

clue.text: Pakistani cuisine from sea's not cold

indicators.note: not tells us the letter for cold is dropped from the sea's name

parts.note: the Baltic is a sea of northern Europe
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A dish from Pakistan is said to come from a sea that is not chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes C from BALTIC; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of spiced curry cooked in a wok-like pan, associated with Pakistani and Kashmiri cooking.

clue.text: Grandiose disorderly and orderly

indicators.note: disorderly says the letters of grandiose are put out of order

explanation.surface: A paradox: something grand is both messy and tidy at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorderly' rearranges all nine letters of GRANDIOSE; the opposite 'orderly' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arranged neatly and systematically is well structured, the same as orderly.

clue.text: Offer to kick novice

parts.note: to tender is to offer, as with a bid
to foot a ball is to kick it

explanation.surface: Someone proposes giving a beginner a boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenderfoot is a newcomer or beginner, originally a raw settler in the American West.

clue.text: City sport light fawn colour

parts.note: EC is the postal district of the City of London
RU stands for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: Sports kit for a City team in a pale beige shade.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, postcode EC; RU is rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: The unbleached shade of linen, a pale greyish yellow-brown, is named from French for raw.

clue.text: Bridge playing with space for newlywed

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of bridge are played about with

parts.note: room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: A card game with room for a recently married man to join in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges BRIDGE into BRIDEG; 'with' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A man just married, or about to be, is a newlywed husband.

clue.text: Dismiss bank employee

explanation.surface: An instruction to sack a teller.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb it means to discharge an officer in disgrace; as a noun it is the person at a bank counter.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss from military service in disgrace, and the person handling money at a bank counter.

clue.text: Wright made this acrobatic manoeuvre

explanation.surface: A craftsman made this gymnastic move.
explanation.walkthrough: A wright is a craftsman; a wheelwright made wheels for carts. 'Wright' looks like the Wright brothers or a surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel for a horse-drawn vehicle, made by a wheelwright, and a sideways handspring with limbs spread like spokes.

clue.text: Lake is hard to spoil

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A lake proves difficult to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: A TARN is a small mountain lake, a word common in northern England; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To dull or sully something, such as a reputation or silverware, is to damage it.

clue.text: Making a m-mention, very soon

indicators.note: making is read as making something new from these letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A stammering speaker starts to mention something any second now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' rearranges A plus the nine letters of M-MENTION; the stutter supplies the second M.
explanation.definitionFit: Something about to happen shortly happens after the briefest pause, very soon.

clue.text: Bits of applause and waves

explanation.surface: Scattered clapping goes round the audience in waves.
explanation.walkthrough: A ripple of applause is a light spread of clapping; ripples are also small waves on water.
explanation.definitionFit: Light spreading sounds of clapping, and small undulations on a water surface.

clue.text: Release the collection. No charge

parts.note: a set is a collection of things belonging together
something at no charge is free

explanation.surface: Issue the whole collection without cost.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a music release or a free giveaway.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate someone from captivity is to let them go, to release them.

clue.text: Itinerant traders who are on bikes, it's said

indicators.note: it's said tells us to hear the word for cyclists spoken

parts.note: cyclists pushing round the cranks are pedallers

explanation.surface: Travelling salesmen get about by bicycle, so people report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' signals that the word for cyclists sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawkers who travel from place to place selling small goods door to door.

clue.text: Doom-merchant suggests gain

indicators.note: suggests here is read as sounds like, the spoken word for gain hinting at another word

parts.note: a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: A pessimist hints that there's money to be made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suggests' signals that the word for gain sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreteller who predicts disaster is a prophet of doom.

clue.text: Advise of hostilities starting now

parts.note: open hostilities between nations are war

indicators.note: starting picks just the opening letter of the word now

explanation.surface: Give notice that fighting is beginning right away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' takes N from 'now'; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To caution or alert someone in advance is to advise them of danger.

clue.text: Turbulent air over New York -it's wet

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the second
turbulent air is disturbed, so the letters of air are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stormy weather over New York means it's raining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turbulent' rearranges AIR into RAI, which sits 'over' NY in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather full of showers is described as wet.

clue.text: Fortified refuge in which a wrestler is kept?

definitions.text: in which a wrestler is kept?

explanation.surface: A fortress where a grappler is held captive.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word: a wrestler pinned in a powerful grip is held in a strong hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle or fort for defence, and a firm wrestling grip that keeps an opponent down.

clue.text: Dentists first removed signs of damage

indicators.note: removed means these letters are taken out of the word dentists

parts.note: first is written 1st, read as IST with I for one

explanation.surface: The dentists who went first have taken out evidence of harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is 1st, written IST; 'removed' takes IST out of DENTISTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollows knocked into a surface, as on a car, are marks showing harm.

clue.text: Carry out a command and order at start of year

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: at start of picks the opening letter of the word year

explanation.surface: An honour is announced and a command issued at New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: OBE is a British honour, often awarded in the New Year list; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To comply with an instruction is to do as one is told.

clue.text: City neighbour, without love embraces duke wildly

indicators.note: embraces means the shortened word wraps round the letter for duke
wildly says the resulting letters are thrown into a new order
without tells us the letter for love is taken out of neighbour

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone living nearby, short of affection, hugs a nobleman with abandon in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops O from NEIGHBOUR to give NEIGHBUR; it 'embraces' D, and 'wildly' rearranges the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland's capital is a large city on the Firth of Forth.

clue.text: One small account about the Pacific

indicators.note: about is read as round and round, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
AC is the short form of account

explanation.surface: A brief report about the world's largest body of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges ONE plus AC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific is the largest of the world's great seas, an example of the category.

clue.text: Cease to use temporary parking area

explanation.surface: Stop using a roadside stopping place.
explanation.walkthrough: To lay something by is to put it aside; a lay-by is a pull-in beside a British road for stopping briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting something aside unused, and a roadside pull-in where vehicles may stop briefly.

clue.text: Rough calculations of site developed by colleagues

indicators.note: a developed site is reworked, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: colleagues are mates, workmates

explanation.surface: Fellow workers produce approximate figures for building on a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges SITE into ESTI; 'of' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Approximate reckonings of cost or quantity are rough calculations.
